summary: Console quota readout shows refreshed tokens but requests continue 429ing during geo failover
description:
Issue summary:

Customer reports seeing Console quota counter jump back to non-zero (token refill) after a regional failover, but API requests continue to receive 429s for several minutes. This looks like a mismatch between what the Console reports and what edge enforcement is doing.

Impact:
- Large customer ingestion pipelines (TraceScale) experiencing sustained 429s during a geo failover window, causing worker retries to back off and backlog to grow.
- Estimated 30-40% of ingestion workers unable to push data for ~8 minutes during event.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for TraceScale (customer-dedicated-42)
- Primary region: us-east; failover region: eu-west
- Model in use: redwood/llama2-70b text-generation
- Traffic pattern: mixed short streaming sessions + periodic bulk embedding jobs from 200 parallel workers

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Begin bulk ingest from 200 workers aimed at the dedicated endpoint in us-east (sustained throughput).
2) Trigger simulated regional maintenance/failover (istio NLB drain in test) causing traffic to route to eu-west.
3) Watch Console quota readout for the tenant: tokens are shown as refilled at failover time.
4) Observe API responses: significant number of 429s for the same API keys for ~5-10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows token count > 0 (refill occurred).
- Edge proxies in eu-west return 429 with X-RateLimit-* headers indicating zero tokens left or short refill window.
- Server-side logs show duplicate refill events in control plane and stale token-bucket state on some edge nodes.

Expected behavior:
- Console and enforcement should converge: if console shows tokens available, edge enforcement should allow requests up to quota. Failover should not create a period where the control plane and enforcement disagree for more than a few seconds.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Snippets of response headers and timestamps (attached in ticket).
- Trace IDs: ts-20260310-usr-1a2b3c, ts-20260310-usr-4d5e6f

Initial hypothesis:
- During geo failover we emit refill events from the control plane; some edge nodes apply refills while others ignore due to cached bucket state or duplicate accounting. Console reads the control-plane state (post-refill) while enforcement on certain proxies is still operating on stale buckets, leading to temporary 429s despite console showing refill.

2026-03-10 14:22 - Support (Aisha Khan) -> Customer: Recommended immediate mitigation: 1) enable exponential backoff with jitter on workers, 2) temporarily reduce parallelism to 50 workers and re-run, 3) add short warm-up at regional endpoints to avoid synchronized burst post-failover. Customer confirmed they can test reduced concurrency tomorrow morning their time.

2026-03-11 08:47 - SRE (Diego Rivera): Confirmed root-cause pattern: control-plane emits per-tenant refill events during failover, but edge proxies apply them locally and also persist local delta in their in-memory bucket. During rapid duplicate refills (one from control plane and one replay from sync agent on edge) some nodes overwrite in-memory state causing negative delta accounting. This manifests as console reading the canonical store but enforcement reading in-memory transient bucket. Opened PR to add atomic merge and idempotency markers to refill messages.

resolution: Partial workaround applied: enabled conservative refill smoothing for TraceScale and rolled canary of idempotent refill handler to eu-west edge. root_cause: During geo failover duplicate refill events and inconsistent local edge bucket merges produced transient enforcement/state drift. Console reads canonical control-plane state which was updated immediately, but enforcement on some edge nodes used stale or incorrectly merged in-memory bucket states, causing 429s despite console showing tokens available.
workaround: 1) Reduce parallel ingestion concurrency during planned failovers. 2) Add exponential backoff with jitter on client retries. 3) Temporary per-tenant conservative refill smoothing enabled by Support (suppresses immediate duplicate refills).
next_steps: 1) Roll out idempotent refill handler to all edge regions (scheduled 2026-03-13 canary -> 2026-03-14 full). 2) Console UI change: display enforcement sync timestamp and a 'state drift' indicator (product ticket created). 3) Add alert when enforcement/control-plane drift exceeds 2s for any tenant. 4) Postmortem entry to OPS runbook and update failover test harness to include bucket-state consistency checks.
